questions.q: Following are the four molecules "P", "Q", "R" and "S". Which one among the four molecules will react with $\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{Br}_{(\mathrm{aq})}$ at the fastest rate?
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution: Addition of $\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{Br}_{(\mathrm{aq})}$ to alkene follows electrophilic addition mechanism. In the rate determining step a carbocation intermediate is formed. Among $\mathrm{P}, \mathrm{Q}$, R \& S compound Q will form most stable carbocation intermediate since it is resonance stabilized.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements.

Statement I: The presence of weaker π-bonds make alkenes less stable than alkanes

Statement II: The strength of the double bond is greater than that of carbon-carbon single bond.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options : given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
As sigma bond is formed along the internuclear axis it is stronger than pi-bond, and due to the presence of pi-bonds alkenes will be more reactive towards electrophilic reagents.Hence they are less stable than alkanes.

The strength of carbon-carbon double bond is greater than single bond as bond strength is directly proportional to bond order.

Hence, both the statements are correct.

options: A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution: The delocalised π-electron cloud is attracted more strongly by the nuclei of the carbon atoms than the electron cloud localised between two carbon atoms. Therefore, presence of delocalised π-electrons in benzene makes it more stable than the hypothetical cyclohexatriene.

The allylic position is a carbon position present adjacent to the carbon-carbon double bonds. The allylic carbon is attached to a carbon atom that forms a double bond with a different carbon atom. A substitution could be a reaction during which a group in an organic molecule is replaced with another group.

When the halogen concentration is low enough, alkenes containing allylic hydrogen undergo substitution at the allylic position rather than addition at the double bond. The product is an allylic halide (halogen on carbon next to double bond carbons), which is acquired through a radical chain mechanism.

When cyclohexene reacts with Chlorine in the presence of CCl4, the electrophilic addition reaction takes place at double bond, which results in a dichloro product, here it is 1,2-dicholorocyclohexane.

Hence, the correct answer is D.
